title: Top exterior power of a direct sum
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $M$ and $N$ be free $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with bases of $r$ and $s$ elements, and write $\bigwedge^n$ for the $n$-th exterior power [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. The alternating map sending $(m_1\wedge\cdots\wedge m_r)\otimes(n_1\wedge\cdots\wedge n_s)$ to $(m_1,0)\wedge\cdots\wedge(m_r,0)\wedge(0,n_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge(0,n_s)$ induces a canonical $R$-module isomorphism $\bigwedge^{r+s}(M\oplus N)\cong\bigwedge^rM\otimes_R\bigwedge^sN$, where the tensor product is that of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], natural in isomorphisms of $M$ and $N$.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: top exterior powers

proof.text: Choose the displayed bases of $M$ and $N$. By the free-module exterior-power basis statement, the wedges indexed by $r$-element and $s$-element increasing subsets are bases of $\bigwedge^r M$ and $\bigwedge^s N$, while the concatenated basis of $M\oplus N$ gives the corresponding wedge basis of $\bigwedge^{r+s}(M\oplus N)$. By the tensor-product product-basis statement, the tensors of the two first bases form a basis of $\bigwedge^rM\otimes_R\bigwedge^sN$.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: top exterior powers

proof.text: The alternating map in the statement sends each tensor of the source basis to the distinct concatenated wedge in the target basis, with coefficient $+1$. It therefore sends a basis bijectively to a basis and extends uniquely to an $R$-module isomorphism. The construction is the alternating multilinear map induced by the inclusions $M\to M\oplus N$ and $N\to M\oplus N$, so it is the stated canonical map.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: top exterior powers

proof.text: If the bases are changed, the same map is still characterized by sending $m_1\wedge\cdots\wedge m_r$ tensored with $n_1\wedge\cdots\wedge n_s$ to the wedge of their images under the two canonical inclusions: writing each $m_k$ and $n_l$ in the chosen bases and expanding by multilinearity, discarding terms with a repeated factor by alternation and reordering the others with $v\wedge w=-w\wedge v$, gives $m_1\wedge\cdots\wedge m_r=c\,e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_r$ in $\bigwedge^rM$ and $(m_1,0)\wedge\cdots\wedge(m_r,0)=c\,(e_1,0)\wedge\cdots\wedge(e_r,0)$ in $\bigwedge^r(M\oplus N)$ with the same scalar $c\in R$ (the two expansions are term by term identical), and likewise a common scalar $d$ for the $n_l$; so the basis-defined map sends the given tensor to $cd$ times the target basis vector, which is the stated wedge. Hence the basis calculation describes one basis-independent map; applying module isomorphisms to $M$ and $N$ commutes with these inclusions, tensor products, and exterior powers, proving naturality.

lean.statement: theorem existsUnique_topDirectSum {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (r s : ℕ) (_bM : Module.Basis (Fin r) R M) (_bN : Module.Basis (Fin s) R N) : ∃! e : (⋀[R]^(r + s) (M × N)) ≃ₗ[R] ((⋀[R]^r M) ⊗[R] (⋀[R]^s N)), ∀ (m : Fin r → M) (n : Fin s → N), e.symm ((ιMulti R r m) ⊗ₜ[R] (ιMulti R s n)) = ιMulti R (r + s) (Fin.append (fun i ↦ (m i, 0)) (fun j ↦ (0, n j)))
lean.note: The first theorem gives the unique isomorphism characterized by its inverse on pure wedges; the second states naturality for every pair of isomorphisms and every two isomorphisms with that characterization. The binary module direct sum is represented by its standard product model.

reviewed_lean.note: CommRing R; M,N with Module.Basis (Fin r)/(Fin s) = free with r,s-element bases; ⋀[R]^n Mathlib exteriorPower, M×N binary direct sum, ⊗[R] Mathlib; ∃! iso ⋀^(r+s)(M×N) ≃ ⋀^r M ⊗ ⋀^s N with e.symm(ιMulti m ⊗ ιMulti n)=ιMulti(Fin.append (m,0) (0,n)) for all tuples (M factors first, +1); naturality as separate theorem for arbitrary f,g isos and any e,e' with the characterization, checked true without bases (pure tensors of wedges span); edge r=0/s=0, zero ring, char 2 fine; Mathlib ExteriorPower/ExteriorAlgebra has no direct-sum top-degree iso (only CliffordAlgebra graded prodEquiv), existing:false correct
